stories.title: Sindh cabinet decides to make judicial commission's report on Mir Raza's murder public
summary: KARACHI: The Sindh cabinet on Tuesday decided to make the report prepared by a judicial commission formed to investigate the circumstances and possible negligence in businessman Mir Raza Ali’s murder investigation public.
Last week, the commission, headed by Justice Omar Sial of the Sindh High Court (SHC), had handed over the sealed report to the provincial government after examining 49 witnesses during 15 hearings.

The inquiry report along with associated documents was handed over to focal person of the provincial government and additional secretary of home department Javed Ahmed Abro by registrar of the commission Abdul Majid on the premises of the SHC.

stories.title: At SCO, Dar calls for promoting use of national currencies to help offset global economic shocks
summary: Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar on Tuesday encouraged members of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) to use national currencies for “mutual settlement” and establish other financial mechanisms to “offset international financial shocks”.

In the joint communiqué for the Pakistan-chaired 2024 CHG meeting, SCO member states had reaffirmed the need for consistent implementation of a roadmap on gradual increase in the share of national currencies in mutual settlements.
On Sept 30, Dar reviewed preparations for the CHS summit as SCO national coordinators, who were in Islamabad for a meeting, called on him.

stories.title: Defamation tribunal orders Punjab Assembly opposition leader to pay Rs3m to Azma Bokhari
summary: LAHORE: The Punjab Defamation Tribunal on Tuesday ruled in favour of Punjab Information Minister Azma Bokhari in a defamation suit against Punjab Assembly Opposition Leader Moeen Riaz Qureshi, ordering him to pay Rs3 million in general damages.
In January, Bokhari filed the defamation suit against Qureshi seeking damages of Rs800 million.
The information minister had filed the suit following the allegations Qureshi levelled at the time of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa’s then-chief minister Sohail Afridi’s visit to the Punjab Assembly.

stories.title: PM Shehbaz ready to build consensus on counterterrorism if opposition willing to: Sanaullah
summary: Adviser to the Prime Minister on Political Affairs Rana Sanaullah on Tuesday said the federal government was ready to invite all political parties and build consensus on counterterrorism.

The PM’s aide’s remarks come after the Centre imposed emergency and governor’s rule in KP on October 11, citing the PTI-led provincial government’s “deliberate disengagement” from the fight against terrorism.
The minister said controlling terrorism in KP was practically impossible without the provincial government’s full cooperation with federal institutions, the Pakistan Army and security agencies.

stories.title: Rubio lands in India for 'trade diplomacy'
summary: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio arrived in India on Tuesday, his second official visit to the country this year, as he pursues an Asian tour blending diplomacy and trade.

Rubio visited Uzbekistan, where he called for stronger partnerships with Central Asian countries, before landing in Mumbai for talks with Foreign Minister Subrahmanyam Jaishankar and meetings with business leaders.
The two countries reached an interim trade agreement in February aimed at reducing US tariffs on Indian goods.

stories.title: As France erupts, Europe's far right gains from fuel-price anger ahead of elections
summary: As soaring fuel prices squeeze household budgets and businesses across Europe, cost-of-living pressures are driving unrest and giving fresh momentum to far-right parties ahead of elections next year in countries including France, Italy and Poland.

Politicians on both the hard right and hard left have increasingly argued that restoring energy ties with Russia would help lower costs, challenging Europe’s mainstream consensus on support for Ukraine.
Le pen makes fuel prices a campaign issue The latest energy shock comes after years of economic strain following the pandemic and the fallout from Russia’s 2022 invasion of Ukraine.

stories.title: Health ministry gets Momin Agha as 9th secretary in 19 months
summary: ISLAMABAD: The health ministry has again gotten a new secretary, with the Establishment Division notifying Momin Agha as the new administrative head.

According to a notification issued by the Establishment Division on Monday, available with Dawn, Agha “has been transferred and posted as secretary health with immediate effect and until further orders”.
Agha was removed as petroleum secretary in January 2026 and directed to report to the Establishment Division without a further posting.

stories.title: PHC issues notices in petitions challenging governor’s rule, emergency in KP; hearing adjourned till Nov 10
summary: PESHAWAR: The Peshawar High Court (PHC) on Tuesday issued notices to the federal and Khyber Pakhtunkhwa governments in several petitions challenging the imposition of emergency and governor’s rule in the province on Oct 11.

Barrister Sameer argued that a resolution passed by the provincial assembly was mandatory for imposing governor’s rule and emergency. “No approval was obtained from the provincial assembly,” he told the court.
Following the imposition of emergency and governor’s rule in the province, the federal government formed an 11-member technocratic KP Advisory Council.

stories.title: Car driver held for crushing underage worker to death in Multan
summary: LAHORE: Multan police arrested a suspect involved in killing his underage worker by hitting him with his car in DHA on Monday.
Later, DHA police registered a murder case on behalf of the state and arrested the suspect who was identified as Tauqeer Nazir.
DIES IN CUSTODY: A suspect arrested in a cheque dishonour case died in alleged custody of the Defence police station here on Monday.

stories.title: Maldives president arrives in Pakistan for three-day visit
summary: Maldives President Dr Mohamed Muizzu arrived in Islamabad on Tuesday on a three-day visit to Pakistan, state-run Radio Pakistan reported.

Meanwhile, the Maldivian delegation, led by Foreign Minister Iruthisham Adam and comprising cabinet ministers and senior officials, arrived in Islamabad earlier on Tuesday ahead of President Muizzu’s arrival, the Foreign Office (FO) said in a statement.
In 2015, former Maldivian president Abdulla Yameen Abdul Gayoom undertook a two-day state visit to Pakistan on May 6-7 at the invitation of then-premier Nawaz Sharif.

stories.title: France to impose new curfews where necessary: PM
summary: France will impose new curfews in areas where needed on Tuesday, Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu said, adding that the measures introduced in several cities the previous day had “helped keep the night calm”.

Several cities, including Paris, the southwestern city of Bordeaux and Nice on the French Riviera, introduced partial curfews on Monday in response to urban unrest that followed weeks of student demonstrations over poor learning conditions in high schools.

In Lyon, despite a ban on demonstrations, around 500 people gathered on Monday evening outside the tourism office that was set on fire, to show support for shopkeepers affected by looting, according to organisers.

stories.title: Alberta votes to remain part of Canada
summary: Alberta residents voted to remain part of Canada in the province’s first-ever referendum on separation, in a much-needed win for Prime Minister Mark Carney as he attempts to unify the country amid a trade war with the US.
Alberta Premier Danielle Smith announced the referendum in May, saying it was time to have a vote, understand the will of Albertans on this subject, and move on.
First Nations groups have also objected to the idea of an independent Alberta, as their land treaties with Ottawa predate the province’s creation within Canada.

stories.title: Declared dead: Indian voters fight to get back on electoral rolls
summary: The 53-year-old tailor is among 130 million names removed from India’s electoral rolls under a voter roll revision that has sparked mass protests and posed the biggest challenge to Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s government.

The Special Intensive Revision (SIR) has led to removals for reasons ranging from “logical discrepancies” to people being recorded as dead, leaving many such as Prasad struggling to get more than just their voting status restored.

Register as a new voter Following weeks of protests, the Election Commission ordered fresh verification in some states, including Delhi, and Prasad said officials had assured him his name would be restored.

stories.title: Health authorities dismiss reports of insulin shortage, cite unavailability of one brand
summary: ISLAMABAD: Authorities on Tuesday denied reports of a widespread insulin shortage in the country, saying that only one brand was unavailable due to international supply constraints.

The health ministry and the Drug Regulatory Authority of Pakistan (Drap) maintained that alternatives for the unavailable brand remained available in the market. “Insulin glulisine (Apidra, Sanofi) is currently unavailable due to international supply constraints.

In August 2025, the Pakistan Medical Association (PMA) raised alarm over “an unprecedented” and severe shortage of essential medicines across the country and warned that the crisis threatened the lives of millions of patients.

stories.title: US bars IT firm from sponsoring green cards, imposes $2m settlement
summary: WASHINGTON: The United States has barred California-based technology company Cloudera Inc. from participating in the employment-based green card process for two years and secured a $2 million settlement over allegations that it discriminated against qualified American workers.

It resolves a lawsuit filed by the Justice Department in April, alleging that Cloudera violated the Immigration and Nationality Act by discriminating against American workers while recruiting for seven positions under the Permanent Labour Certification, or PERM, programme.
During the debarment period, the company cannot participate in the PERM programme to sponsor foreign workers for employment-based green cards.

stories.title: Toll plazas still incomplete as Rawalpindi Ring Road cost escalates to Rs50.4bn
summary: RAWALPINDI: Despite the cost of Rawalpindi Ring Road project rising from Rs47 billion to Rs50.4 billion for the third time since work began, the construction of toll plazas still remains incomplete.
He said if the land acquisition amount was added to the construction cost the total cost of the project would increase to Rs57 billion.
He said toll plaza booths were being installed in Baanth and Thalian and Punjab Ring Road Authority offices were being established along with the construction of residential areas for officials.

stories.title: Diomande starting to shine as Leipzig visit
summary: When Real Madrid splashed a club record 140 million euros ($157m) to sign Yan Diomande from RB Leipzig this summer, it was because of his clear potential to become one of the game's stars, as showcased at the 2026 World Cup.

"At Real Madrid, the demands are very high... but he had a great game, he's growing." 'I will die trying' Diamonds form under pressure, and thus far in his career Diomande has handled it on and off the pitch.
Diomande helped Leipzig reach the Champions League with 12 goals and eight assists, and he was named "rookie of the year" in the Bundesliga, before his Madrid move.

stories.title: CDA’s act of dumping waste between I-10, I-11 in Islamabad slammed in NA
summary: The minister lamented that residents of Islamabad, including those living along Margalla Road, and F series sectors pay nothing against waste collection.

He said that special focus was being paid on solid waste and CDA, through a Turkish company had recently launched a project to clean Islamabad’s rural areas and collect garbage, providing a long-awaited municipal service to residents.
He said that special focus was now being paid on sector development, adding that during the last one month commercial area of sector E-12 was retrieved by CDA worth Rs200 billion.

stories.title: Health secretary takes stock of Pims’ administrative, operational challenges
summary: Pims Executive Director Tanwir Khaliq, Joint Executive Director and heads of various departments accompanied the secretary and briefed the secretary about the hospital’s operational matters and ongoing initiatives.
Arthroplasty Workshop Concludes Meanwhile, the Department of Orthopaedic Surgery at the Pims organised a two-day live knee and hip arthroplasty workshop.
He stated that the workshop aimed to train young surgeons according to international standards, enabling patients to access high-quality, affordable joint replacement surgery within the country.

stories.title: PTI lawmaker arrested in raid on Bannu madressah
summary: The PTI condemned the lawmaker’s arrest and said that the ‘Form 47 government’ in the Centre was undermining the Constitution, the rule of law and democratic principles.
The PTI said that governments derived their authority from the public mandate and had a fundamental responsibility to protect the people’s rights rather than intimidate political opponents.
The PTI demanded that the legal grounds for MNA Shah’s arrest and details of his current whereabouts be made public immediately.

stories.title: Powerloom workers protest ‘police torture’ in Faisalabad
summary: Addressing the protesters, Labour Qaumi Movement chairman Baba Latif Insari alleged that powerloom worker Ghulam Mustafa had demanded payment of his wages, prompting the police to raid his house allegedly to please the factory owner.
According to a press release, an inquiry conducted by a superintendent of police found SI Hakim Ali guilty of misconduct.
ACCIDENT: A woman was killed and her husband critically injured when a motorcycle-rickshaw hit them in Gojra on Sunday night.

stories.title: Peshawar High Court hears petitions against governor’s rule today
summary: Barrister Gohar on Monday filed an application in the high court, seeking permission to add two further prayers in his constitutional petition.
The applicant stated that on Oct 14 the National Assembly and the Senate passed separate resolutions approving the proclamation of emergency “under second proviso of clause (1) of Article 232”.

He stated that on Oct 15 the Parliament in a joint sitting passed two further resolutions, the first approving the proclamation of emergency under clause (7) of Article 232, and the second approving the proclamation under clause (3) of Article 234.

stories.title: Sindh senior minister Sharjeel stresses need to integrate all BRT projects
summary: Speaking about the number of passengers travelling on the Green Line, Mr Memon said that figures were not presented merely to make statements.
When the Green Line was under the federal government’s control, approximately 50,000 passengers travelled on it daily.
He said that approximately 90,000 passengers were now travelling on the Green Line daily.

stories.title: Robbers take away Rs6m from petrol pump cashier in Karachi
summary: KARACHI: Robbers took away Rs6 million from the cashier of a petrol pump near Mosamiyat in Gulistan-i-Jauhar on Monday, police said.
The police said as the robbers were fleeing, the guard opened fire, but the bullet hit a passer-by, later identified as Mohammed Afzal, 48.
The suspects managed to escape from the spot, leaving behind their motorcycle and a pistol.

stories.title: Work on four garbage stations in final stages: Sindh CM
summary: The chief minister formally inaugurated the project by cutting the ribbon and initiating waste disposal at the site.
Murad inaugurates first phase of Sindh’s new engineered landfill site at Jam Chakro The four GTS were earlier informal dumping grounds being modernised under the World Bank-funded SWEEP project.

The chief minister said that the landfill project was expected to generate carbon credits worth around $20 million, marking a major shift towards scientific and environmentally sustainable waste disposal in Karachi.

stories.title: Calls to relocate stray dogs grow as two more die of rabies in Sindh
summary: Dr Azhar, who is also part of a civil society initiative against rabies, emphasised that the problem was not rabies but the stray dogs attacking people. “In 99 per cent of cases in our environment, rabies is a consequence of a dog bite.

Dr Azhar also referred to a recent Indus Hospital study, which has shown a high prevalence of rabies virus in Karachi’s street dogs. “The findings pointed to substantial virus burden in stray dogs that underlines the need for urgent action to control the dog population,” he said.

The research, titled ‘Detection of Rabies Virus RNA in Dog-Bite Wounds in a Rabies-Endemic Area: Evidence from an Observational Cohort Study,’ revealed a strikingly high level of rabies virus circulation in the local canine population, with the virus detected in 64pc of samples.

stories.title: Karachi's Nehr-i-Khayyam rehabilitation to improve Clifton environment, says minister
summary: KARACHI: In a bid to allay concerns of residents about covering Nehr-i-Khayyam with concrete, Local Government Minister Nasir Shah on Monday said that the project aimed at improving the drainage system and overall environment of Clifton.
Also on Monday, Sindh Chief Secretary Asif Hyder Shah presided over a meeting to review the Nehr-i-Khayyam project.
The Local Government Department informed the meeting that the project focused on preserving its historical and environmental significance and helping reduce urban flooding.

stories.title: Govt calls on all political parties to unite, forge consensus against terrorism and set aside differences
summary: The government on Tuesday urged all political parties to set aside their differences and forge a consensus on a joint strategy to combat terrorism, saying it was a national issue that required collective efforts and a unified response. “This is a national issue.

Sanaullah said terrorism was a national issue that required all political parties to set aside their differences and agree on a joint strategy, adding that the government was prepared to engage with the opposition to resolve the matter.

After negotiations failed, the federal government imposed emergency and governor’s rule in K-P on October 11, citing the deteriorating security situation and what it said was a lack of cooperation from the provincial administration in the fight against terrorism.

stories.title: Two sentenced in FC personnel’s murder case in Gilgit-Baltistan
summary: GILGIT: An anti-terrorism court (ATC) in Gilgit-Baltistan on Monday sentenced the prime accused to death and his accomplice to life imprisonment in the murder case of a Frontier Corps (FC) personnel at a forest checkpost in Thore, Diamer.
ATC Judge Rehmat Shah heard the case involving the murder of FC personnel Muhammad Gul Sher at the Thore checkpost in Diamer.
After finding the accused guilty, the court sentenced the prime accused, Usman Shafi, to death and his accomplice, Gulzar, to life imprisonment.

stories.title: 20 abducted police recruits ‘recovered safely’ in Kalat
summary: QUETTA: The 20 police recruits from the Kalat Police Training Centre, who were abducted by unidentified men on Friday, have been safely recovered, officials told Dawn.
The recruits, who were kidnapped while en route to Noshki from Kalat in a private van, were recovered from the Mangochar area of Kalat district, sources said.
A senior police officer told Dawn that “all personnel are safe and sound”.

stories.title: Dispute over Zangali checkpost disrupts Torkham operations
summary: KHYBER: The repatriation of Afghan families was suspended for about two hours, while staff members of government offices were asked to leave after a dispute over the repair or construction of a controversial checkpost on the Afghan side of the Torkham border emerged on Monday.
Sabir Khan, a resident of Torkham, told Dawn that the repatriation of Afghans resumed after about two hours and the Customs and immigration offices reopened.

Customs and immigration officials later confirmed that their operations, including the clearance of belongings of returning Afghan families and immigration procedures, had resumed after the Afghan authorities suspended construction work on the disputed checkpost.

stories.title: Punjab Information Minister Azma Bokhari wins Rs84m defamation case against opposition leader
summary: Punjab Information Minister Azma Bokhari won a defamation case against Punjab Assembly Opposition Leader Moeen Riaz Qureshi on Tuesday, with the court ruling in her favour in an Rs84 million damages suit over allegations he made against her during a television programme.

Azma had filed the suit before the Lahore Defamation Tribunal under the Defamation Act, seeking Rs84 million in damages over Qureshi’s allegations concerning the visit of the Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa (K-P) chief minister to the Punjab Assembly.
Azma said Qureshi had alleged that the information minister brought more than 100 paid persons into the Punjab Assembly during the K-P chief minister’s visit.

stories.title: PTI remains split over future course of action
summary: Some participants alleged that Sohail Afridi was responsible for the failure, but others questioned the role of the PTI core and political committees and said why the core committee took seven days to call its meeting.

The participant told Dawn that members had shown concerns about why TTAP was being allowed to open party offices at district level and asked if PTI will contest the next election under the banner of TTAP, but Barrister Gohar denied any such development.

PTI Central Information Secretary Sheikh Waqas Akram, told Dawn that he can only say that during the meeting, detailed discussions were held. “The discussion will be helpful in collective decision-making for the future and it will also be helpful for policy-making,” he said.

stories.title: PSX edges up on buying in key sectors
summary: The benchmark KSE-100 Index was trading at 166,130.38 at 12.28pm, up 164.30 points, or 0.10%.
The market opened on a positive note, with the index gaining 312.38 points, or 0.19% to reach 166,278.46 points.
Read: PSX slips 454 points as investors struggle to find direction Early buying lifted the benchmark, which subsequently pared some gains before recovering modestly.

stories.title: Anger at rising fuel prices bolsters Europe's far right as unrest sweeps France
summary: Rising fuel costs are piling pressure on households, businesses and governments across Europe, fuelling cost-of-living protests and bolstering the far right ahead of elections next year in countries including France, Italy and Poland.

As soaring fuel prices squeeze household budgets and businesses across Europe, cost-of-living pressures are driving unrest and giving fresh momentum to far-right parties ahead of elections next year in countries including France, Italy and Poland.

Politicians on both the hard right and hard left have increasingly argued that restoring energy ties with Russia would help lower costs, challenging Europe's mainstream consensus on support for Ukraine.

stories.title: Govt unveils hi-tech system to manage loadshedding
summary: According to him, the APMS will identify specific transformers in high-theft areas, enabling targeted disconnections so that thousands of paying consumers on an entire feeder are not penalised for the actions of electricity thieves.

After replacement, the APMS would be synced with the smart meters and start monitoring the real-time consumption of electricity users. “Suppose there are 200 consumers receiving power from one transformer in any area.

With the APMS, the area would be narrowed from the feeder to the transformer (150 to 200 consumers),” he said, adding that this would help Lesco stop power theft and reduce line losses more effectively.

stories.title: Houthis inflict major losses on Yemeni forces
summary: Saree said the attacks targeted King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh, Saudi Aramco facilities in Yanbu on the Red Sea coast and the Shaybah oil field near the United Arab Emirates border.

Saree claimed the three-stage attack on the Riyadh airport achieved “accurate and direct” strikes in retaliation for more than 200 Saudi airstrikes and missile attacks on Houthi-held areas over the previous 48 hours.

Work from home Amid the repeated cross-border strikes, government agencies in Riyadh instructed employees to work from home starting from Monday, according to a worker and two consultants who spoke to AFP.

stories.title: Pakistan reel at 94-4 as England bowlers strike in Rawalpindi
summary: England captain Harry Brook won the toss and elected to field at Rawalpindi Cricket Stadium, and his bowlers responded by removing three of Pakistan’s top-order batters before spinner Adil Rashid dismissed Salman Ali Agha to deepen the hosts’ troubles.
Pakistan began the tri-series with a 37-run win over Sri Lanka and will be looking to recover from the early collapse to post a competitive total against England.

Pakistan captain Shaheen Shah Afridi said his team would assess the conditions during the opening overs before looking to post a competitive total. “I hope we will be able to post a good total,” Afridi said.

stories.title: 15-year-old allegedly run over by employer after workplace dispute in Multan
summary: According to the report, they told police that Waseem had passed by shortly before the incident, saying that the suspects wanted to kill him and that he was running to save his life.
Haider said the orphanage had sent Waseem to Tauqeer after making inquiries about the contractor, who had a team of around 40 to 45 boys.
Waseem was later admitted to the orphanage by his grandfather and uncle, he said. “Tauqeer deliberately killed my nephew.

stories.title: KP records 100 dengue cases in 24 hours
summary: PESHAWAR: Khyber Pakhtunkhwa on Monday recorded around 100 new dengue cases in the last 24 hours, the highest daily tally this year, as the province continues to pass through the high-risk month of October.
The report said the health department was carrying out measures to control and prevent dengue in Kohat where a sharp rise in cases had put pressure on hospitals.
The experts said the health department had been implementing the dengue action plan since 2017, updating it every year with changes to the previous version.
